_meta.title: Session 36 — 10-link multi-source analysis: AgentDoG 1.5 + Gemini Embedding 2 + LocateAnything-3B + LFM2.5-8B-A1B + Offensive Cyber Time Horizons + AutoScientists completeness
_meta.context: Analyzed 10 user-provided links (PDFs + web pages + tables). Resolved to: 4 NEW models, 18 NEW benchmarks, 46 scores. Each source's key result tables verified by DIRECT WebFetch of the arxiv HTML / source page (not agent-relayed). De-dup notes: arxiv 2605.27365 == NVIDIA LocateAnything HF/project page (same release); arxiv 2605.26302 == agingbench.github.io (AgingBench, already registered S30 — re-checked, SKIPPED: no composite metric, leaderboard is non-frontier mid/small models only); arxiv 2605.28655 (AutoScientists) already had 3 scores S33 — added 5 new table-based sub-scores.
_meta.rule: STRICT-ATTRIBUTION. Every triple verified by direct WebFetch of the source table. Comparison-model scores ingested ONLY on NEWLY-CREATED benchmarks (no existing data to clobber via loader REPLACE). LFM2.5 comparison models (gpt-oss-20b, qwen3.5-4b) added only on the new aa_omniscience_index bench, NOT on existing math_500/ifeval/aime (would overwrite first-party scores with Liquid-blog-reported figures). EXCLUDED (figure-only, not in any text table): AgentDoG ATBench-Claw/ATBench-Codex per-model scores (Fig 7); AutoScientists nanochat val_bpb 0.9730/0.9777 (Fig 4b + main text only — existing 0.973 left untouched). AgingBench SKIPPED (registered S30, no composite, non-frontier board).

models.name: AgentDoG 1.5-4B
models._note: Lightweight agentic-trajectory safety/security guardrail judge (Qwen3.5-4B base). arxiv 2605.29801. Family also has 0.8B/2B/8B + a unified '-U' variant (4B-U leads ATBench at 78.4 Acc). Code: github.com/AI45Lab/AgentDoG.

models.name: Gemini Embedding 2
models._note: Native multimodal embedding model from Gemini (3072-dim, MRL). arxiv 2605.27295. Unified V/A/I/T embedding space; SOTA on multimodal retrieval + MTEB(Code) + CoIR.

models.name: LocateAnything-3B
models._note: 3B vision-language grounding/detection model (MoonViT + Qwen2.5-3B). arxiv 2605.27365. Parallel Box Decoding (PBD) ~2.5x throughput. SOTA ScreenSpot-Pro GUI grounding 60.3 at 3B. HF: nvidia/LocateAnything-3B (non-commercial license).

models.name: LFM2.5-8B-A1B
models._note: On-device MoE reasoning model: 8B total / ~1B active, 128K context (up from 32K in LFM2-8B-A1B), 128K vocab. Matches Gemma-4-26B-class quality at ~1B active params; 253 tok/s on M5 Max. Distinct from existing liquid-ai/lfm2-8b-a1b (LFM2) and lfm2.5-1.2b.

benchmarks.name: R-Judge
benchmarks.description: Agent-safety judge benchmark — classify whether an agent interaction trajectory is safe/unsafe. Reported as Accuracy (also Prec/Rec/F1). Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: ATBench
benchmarks.description: Agent-Trajectory safety benchmark (1,000 trajectories) — binary safe/unsafe classification of agentic execution traces. Accuracy. Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: MTEB (Code)
benchmarks.description: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark — code retrieval subset. Mean score across code-retrieval tasks. Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: CoIR
benchmarks.description: Code Information Retrieval benchmark — mean across code search/retrieval tasks. Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: MTEB (Multilingual)
benchmarks.description: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark — multilingual track, mean (task). Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: MSEB
benchmarks.description: Massive Sound Embedding Benchmark — audio retrieval, average mrr@10. Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: RefCOCOg
benchmarks.description: Referring expression comprehension — localize the object described by a natural-language expression. Reported as F1 (test split). Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: LVIS (detection)
benchmarks.description: Large-Vocabulary Instance Segmentation detection — open-vocabulary object detection mean F1 (avg of F1@0.5 and F1@0.95). Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: COCO (detection)
benchmarks.description: COCO object detection — mean F1 (avg of F1@0.5 and F1@0.95) in the LocateAnything grounding eval protocol. Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: Offensive Cyber Time Horizon (P50)
benchmarks.description: METR-style time-horizon extended to offensive cyber: the human-expert task duration (hours) at which a model reaches 50% success, IRT-fit over 316 tasks across 7 cyber benchmarks (CyBench/InterCode-CTF/NL2Bash/CyBashBench/NYUCTF/CVEBench/CyberGym). Higher=more capable.

benchmarks.name: Offensive Cyber Success Rate
benchmarks.description: Overall task success rate across the 316-task offensive-cyber suite (7 benchmarks). Higher=better. Lyptus Research time-horizon study.

benchmarks.name: AA-Omniscience Index
benchmarks.description: Artificial Analysis Omniscience Index — knowledge-recall reliability score that penalizes hallucination; can be negative. Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: BioML-Bench (Biomedical Imaging)
benchmarks.description: BioML-Bench biomedical-imaging domain — leaderboard percentile achieved by an autonomous research agent. Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: BioML-Bench (Drug Discovery)
benchmarks.description: BioML-Bench drug-discovery domain — leaderboard percentile. Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: BioML-Bench (Protein Engineering)
benchmarks.description: BioML-Bench protein-engineering domain — leaderboard percentile. Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: BioML-Bench (Single Cell Omics)
benchmarks.description: BioML-Bench single-cell-omics domain — leaderboard percentile. Higher=better.

benchmarks.name: TDC hERG
benchmarks.description: Therapeutics Data Commons hERG cardiotoxicity blocker classification — AUROC. Higher=better.
